temperature_range: 50–75 °C for precursor temperature, 250–350 °C for deposition temperature
summary: The study reports the successful Atomic Layer Deposition (ALD) of transition metals including iron, cobalt, nickel, and copper, as well as their oxides, using complementary and self-limiting reactions with molecular hydrogen or water vapour. The process involves the use of volatile metal acetamidinates as precursors, which react with hydrogen or water to form metal films or oxides. The ALD process ensures uniform and conformal coatings, even in high aspect ratio structures.
evidence: Atomic layer deposition (ALD) is a process for depositing highly uniform and conformal thin films by alternating exposures of a surface to vapours of two chemical reactants. ALD processes have been successfully demonstrated for many metal compounds, but for only very few pure metals. Here we demonstrate processes for the ALD of transition metals including copper, cobalt, iron and nickel. Homoleptic N,N′-dialkylacetamidinato metal compounds and molecular hydrogen gas were used as the reactants. Their surface reactions were found to be complementary and self-limiting, thus providing highly uniform thicknesses and conformal coating of long, narrow holes.
